newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: FORECAST-Sime seen posting strong profit.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Sime seen posting strong profit.

text.p: Malaysian conglomerate Sime Darby Bhd is likely to post strong half-year earnings led by contribution from its latest jewel, Sime Bank, analysts said on Thursday.
Sime is due to release its financial results for the half-year to December 31, 1996 on Saturday.
"Results should be strong. There's no reason for Sime Darby not to do well, given the contribution from Sime Bank," said Patrick Tan, assistant director of HG Asia.
The brokerage house is estimating a half-year net profit of 424 million ringgit ($172 million), up 48.9 percent from 284.7 million ringgit in the previous corresponding period.
Sime's acquisition of a 60 percent stake in Sime Bank, formerly United Malayan Banking Corp (UMBC) and Malaysia's fourth largest banking group, was completed in April last year.
Analysts said expectations of a strong rebound in the performance of Sime's Hong Kong and Singapore operations should also contribute to a stronger growth for the diversified multinational this year.
Sime Darby Hong Kong and Sime Singapore Ltd reported sharp falls in net profits last year due to poor trading margins.
"Singapore and Hong Kong should stage strong rebounds against the first half of last year," Tan said.
Analysts said strong contributions were also expected from the group's property and tractor divisions.
"Tractors Malaysia Holdings, Sime UEP Properties and Sime Bank will be the major profit contributors," said Seow Choong Liang, head of Kleinwort Benson Research (Malaysia).

Earnings at Sime's plantations division, however, could be affected by lower crude palm oil prices during the period, analysts said. "The plantations division's profit will be at best flat," said Tan of HG Asia.

A survey of 30 stockbroking houses showed a forecast net profit of 817.0 million ringgit for the year ending June 30, 1997, giving the stock a 35.2 cents net earnings per share. Net profit in the 1995/96 financial year was 682.5 million ringgit, the group's ninth year of record profit.
"Our forecast for this year is 866 million ringgit which is at the higher end of consensus. We had always been bullish on Sime," Seow said.
At the current price of 9.50 ringgit a share, Kleinwort Benson is calling a "buy on weakness" on Sime stock.
"Sime was never really a sell. It's a core holding stock," Seow added.
